advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Route the discovery-time HCL parses in build_snapshot (_child_dirs / _reverse_caller_dirs) through the worker boundary (or document that discovery parses run in-process and are NOT fail-open, and reconcile ADR 0111 §1).
evidence: terraform_index.py:129-133 `_child_dirs` does `from . import terraform_parse as tp` then `_safe_parse(root, rel_file, tp)`
terraform_index.py:177-183 `_safe_parse` calls `tp.parse_document(text)` directly (no worker)
terraform_tools.py open_session: `snapshot = tfi.build_snapshot(str(root), selected)` runs in the main process, not run_in_worker

ADR 0111 §1: 'The only subprocess is the existing grounding worker boundary ... which runs the pure parse fail-open so a parser hang or segfault degrades to an abstention rather than crashing the review' and 'hcl2/lark are imported lazily (only inside the worker ...)'

terraform_parse.py module docstring: 'the single module-level callable the grounding worker boundary ... invokes in a spawn subprocess — so a hang/segfault in the C-ish parser becomes a fail-open abstain, never a host crash'
advisory.finding: build_snapshot parses .tf files via terraform_parse.parse_document (which lazily imports hcl2/lark) in the MAIN process during forward-child (_child_dirs) and reverse-caller (_reverse_caller_dirs) discovery, violating the documented invariant that the HCL parser is only ever invoked inside the fork/spawn worker boundary. A parser hang or segfault during snapshot discovery therefore occurs in-process and would hang/crash the review rather than degrade to a fail-open abstention.
scenarios: A malformed/pathological .tf during module-closure discovery makes hcl2/lark hang or segfault while building the snapshot inside open_session
A large repo's reverse-caller scan parses many files in-process

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add tests driving the terraform session's worker boundary into timeout / version_skew / other and assert (evidence.reason, receipt.reason_detail) == (timeout, worker_timeout), (version_skew, parser_version), (other, worker_failure).
evidence: terraform_tools.py _run_parse: `if rr.abstained: return {}, tr.WORKER_REASON_DETAIL.get(rr.abstain_reason or "other", "worker_failure")`
terraform_receipt.py WORKER_REASON_DETAIL maps `timeout`->`worker_timeout`, `parse_error`->`invalid_input`, `version_skew`->`parser_version`, `other`->`worker_failure`
search_files for `worker_timeout` / `version_skew` / `WORKER_REASON_DETAIL` under tests/ returns no terraform-session hits
docs/grounding.md outcomes table lists `worker timeout | timeout / worker_timeout`, `wrong parser version | version_skew / parser_version`, `worker other failure | other / worker_failure`
advisory.finding: The worker fail-open abstention translation (WORKER_REASON_DETAIL: timeout->worker_timeout, version_skew->parser_version, other->worker_failure) added in terraform_tools._run_parse has no test. docs/grounding.md declares worker timeout (`timeout`/`worker_timeout`), wrong parser version (`version_skew`/`parser_version`), and worker other failure (`other`/`worker_failure`) as distinct closed outcomes, but no test drives run_in_worker into any abstained state, so a regression that mis-maps or collapses these would pass.
advisory.suggested_fix: Monkeypatch rebar.grounding.harness.run_in_worker (or _installed_version for the version-skew arm) to return an abstained RunResult with each abstain_reason, and assert the resulting Result's evidence.reason / receipt.reason_detail.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test where an in-snapshot .tf file is unreadable (e.g. chmod 0 or a directory in its place) and assert the query abstains with reason_detail == 'unreadable_file'.
evidence: terraform_tools.py _parse_file: `except OSError: return {}, "unreadable_file"`
search_files for `unreadable_file` under tests/ returns only an unrelated review-bot test
docs/grounding.md: `| unreadable capture | parse_error / unreadable_file |`
advisory.finding: The `unreadable_file` abstention branch newly added in terraform_tools._parse_file (OSError on read_bytes -> 'unreadable_file') has no test, though docs/grounding.md lists `unreadable capture | parse_error / unreadable_file` as a closed outcome.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a resolve_reference test on `module.<name>.<out>` where the module's `source` is an interpolated string (`"${var.x}"`) asserting reason_detail == 'dynamic_source' (and cover computed_value / unknown_tfvars).
evidence: _resolve_module_output: `if call.get("dynamic"): return self._abstain("resolve_reference", query, "dynamic_source", from_dir)`
test_terraform_tools.py covers only provider_attribute (line 165) and splat_index (line 177) among the ambiguous prohibitions
docs/grounding.md lists `dynamic source/expression | ambiguous / dynamic_source | dynamic_expression`, `computed value | ambiguous / computed_value`, `unknown tfvars | ambiguous / unknown_tfvars`
advisory.finding: Documented V1 prohibition abstentions dynamic_source, computed_value, and unknown_tfvars are untested. Only provider_attribute and splat_index abstains have tests. dynamic_source in particular gates the newly added _resolve_module_output branch when a module's source is interpolated (dynamic).
advisory.suggested_fix: Write an infra/main.tf with `module "vpc" { source = "${var.env}/vpc" }`, resolve `module.vpc.vpc_id`, and assert evidence.reason == 'ambiguous' and receipt.reason_detail == 'dynamic_source'.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Validate an abstain receipt against schemas.TERRAFORM_GROUNDING_RECEIPT in at least one abstain test (e.g. the no_unique_address or path_outside_snapshot case).
evidence: Only line 118 calls `schemas.validator(schemas.TERRAFORM_GROUNDING_RECEIPT).validate(r)`, inside test_lookup_declaration_emits_a_schema_valid_receipt (a refuted outcome)

abstain_receipt in terraform_receipt.py sets `outcome='abstain', reason=..., reason_detail=..., result_digest=_abstain_result_digest(...)` — a different field profile than refuted_receipt (reason=None, reason_detail=None)
schemas/__init__.py adds TERRAFORM_GROUNDING_RECEIPT to INPUT_SCHEMAS (line 251), which test_schema_coverage.py exempts from OUTPUT_SCHEMAS wiring — no coverage test validates instances
advisory.finding: The abstain receipt is never validated against the TERRAFORM_GROUNDING_RECEIPT schema. Only the refuted receipt is schema-validated (line 118); the many abstain tests assert reason_detail but no test validates the abstain receipt document, even though it has a materially different shape (populated reason/reason_detail, a different result_digest input set) than the refuted receipt. The schema is in INPUT_SCHEMAS, so the schema-coverage suite does not reach it either.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Bound or batch the per-file worker spawns for an empty-module-hint lookup_declaration (e.g. parse a whole module or the full file set in one worker call) so per-query latency does not scale with repo .tf file count.
evidence: _targets('') returns `sorted(self._snapshot.modules)` (all modules) for an empty hint (terraform_tools.py:238-241)
_find_declaration iterates every target module and calls _parse_module, which loops `for rel_file in self._module_files(module_dir)` calling _parse_file per file (terraform_tools.py:262-274)
_parse_file on a cache miss calls _run_parse -> run_in_worker (terraform_tools.py:288, 295-305)
run_in_worker: 'The default multiprocessing context is ``spawn``, so ``func`` must be a module-level importable callable' — a full interpreter startup per invocation (harness.py:287-291)
_run_parse does not pass mp_context, so every file parse pays the spawn cost; there is no batching of multiple files into a single worker call (terraform_tools.py:295-314)
LIMITS caps files at 5000 and modules at 64 (terraform_index.py LIMITS), so the worst case is bounded but still linear in repo Terraform size per empty-hint query
advisory.finding: An empty-module-hint lookup_declaration spawns one 'spawn'-context worker subprocess per uncached .tf file across ALL snapshot modules, serialized — the per-query cost scales linearly with the repo's in-scope Terraform file count (up to the 5000-file / 64-module LIMITS bound), with a per-spawn worker timeout.
scenarios: An agentic T10 finder issues lookup_declaration with no module_path against a large monorepo containing thousands of .tf files
A review of a Terraform repo near the 5000-file / 64-module bound where the first query cold-fills the parse cache

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm pyproject.toml declares an `[project.optional-dependencies] grounding-terraform = ["python-hcl2==8.1.3"]` (and any needed lark pin) and that it is included in this change.
evidence: docs/grounding.md documents: `pip install 'rebar[grounding-terraform]'   # or: uv sync --extra grounding-terraform`
ADR states: 'The capability is gated behind an OPTIONAL extra (`grounding-terraform`)'
ABSENCE: no pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, or setup.py appears in the 29-file changed-files list
src/rebar/grounding/terraform_receipt.py declares `PARSER_VERSION = "8.1.3"` pinning the parser version in code, which must match the manifest pin
ADR 0111: '`python-hcl2` is Apache-2.0, dependency-light (`lark`)' — introduces transitive dependency lark
ABSENCE: no uv.lock, poetry.lock, or requirements file appears in the 29-file changed-files list
The pin `python-hcl2==8.1.3` is exact but lark is not pinned anywhere in the diff
dropped.finding: The new optional dependency python-hcl2==8.1.3 (and its transitive dependency lark) is referenced throughout the change but NO manifest file (pyproject.toml / setup.cfg) declaring the `grounding-terraform` extra appears in the 29 changed files, so the extra `pip install 'rebar[grounding-terraform]'` and `uv sync --extra grounding-terraform` cannot resolve.
merged_from: No lockfile update (uv.lock / poetry.lock / requirements*.txt) is present in the changed files despite adding python-hcl2==8.1.3 and its transitive lark dependency, risking a lockfile/manifest inconsistency and unpinned transitive provenance.
scenarios: User runs `pip install 'rebar[grounding-terraform]'` and pip errors that the extra does not exist
CI extra-install job fails to resolve grounding-terraform

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify `_capabilities.is_available("grounding_terraform")` is registered to the module provided by the `grounding-terraform` extra (python-hcl2/hcl2) and that the hyphen/underscore forms are reconciled.
evidence: terraform_tools.py: `return _capabilities.is_available("grounding_terraform")`
terraform_tools.py: `_EXTRA = "grounding-terraform"` (hyphen) is defined but the probe uses the underscore form
docs/grounding.md install uses hyphen: `rebar[grounding-terraform]`
dropped.finding: The capability key used at runtime (`is_available("grounding_terraform")`) uses an underscore while the extra/install name uses a hyphen (`grounding-terraform`); this mapping must be verified against the capability registry so the extra name and probe cannot drift.
scenarios: The capability registry keys the probe by a spec/module name that does not match, so available() always returns False even with the extra installed

evidence: terraform_parse.py:_declarations correlates `spans` (tree document order) with `data.get(btype)` (per-type list) using `counters[btype]` — order-sensitive added logic
test_terraform_tools.py:96 asserts only `e["location"]["line_start"] == 5` for one resource
search_files for `terraform_parse` / `parse_document` under tests returned `(no matches)` — no direct test module for the parser

A named violating input: a single .tf with `variable "a"` at lines 1-3 then `output "o"` at 5-7 then `variable "b"` at 9-11 — a lookup of `variable.b` must report line_start=9, and nothing asserts the second same-type block's span is not the first's
dropped.finding: The declaration/span correlation in terraform_parse._declarations (correlating tree-order block spans with per-type hcl2.loads entries via document-order counters) is only exercised by a single line_start==5 assertion on one resource; a document with MULTIPLE blocks of the same type (e.g. two `variable` blocks at different lines) — which is what would expose a mis-correlation between the span list and the loads() per-type list — is never tested, so a swapped/incorrect line span would ship green.
dropped.suggested_fix: Add tests/unit/grounding covering a module with >=2 same-type blocks and assert lookup_declaration reports the correct distinct line_start for each address.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Populate `tfvars[rel_dir].append(rel)` for explicitly selected .tfvars paths in _seed_dirs, or remove the unused tfvars dict / selected_tfvars field if selection is never supported.
evidence: terraform_index.py:226-237 `tfvars: dict[str, list[str]] = {}` ... `if _has_tf_suffix(rel, _TFVARS_SUFFIXES): affected.add(rel_dir); continue` — never writes to `tfvars`
build_snapshot: `selected_tfvars=sorted(tfvars.get(rel_dir, []))` therefore always resolves to []
test only asserts the empty case: tests/unit/grounding/test_terraform_index.py:123 `assert snap.modules["infra"].selected_tfvars == []`
dropped.finding: _seed_dirs constructs and returns a `tfvars` dict but never assigns into it: the `.tfvars` branch only adds the dir to `affected`, so `tfvars` is always empty. Consequently Module.selected_tfvars is always [], and build_snapshot's `sorted(tfvars.get(rel_dir, []))` is dead — an explicitly selected .tfvars path is never recorded, making the selected_tfvars feature non-functional.
scenarios: A caller explicitly selects a .tfvars path expecting it to appear in Module.selected_tfvars

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Bound or short-circuit the reverse-caller scan (e.g. cap files scanned / cache the reverse index) so snapshot builds are not O(all repo .tf) per session.
evidence: terraform_index.py:186-200 `_all_repo_tf_files` os.walks the whole root
terraform_index.py:203-220 `_reverse_caller_dirs` parses every repo tf file via `_safe_parse` for reverse-caller discovery
_closure (terraform_index.py:240) calls _reverse_caller_dirs on each build
dropped.finding: _reverse_caller_dirs walks the ENTIRE repo tree (_all_repo_tf_files) and parses every .tf/.tf.json file on every snapshot build, regardless of how small the selected seed set is. On a large monorepo this parses potentially thousands of files in-process each time a session opens.
scenarios: A large repo with many .tf files opens a T10 grounding session per agent call

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Wire terraform_membership_entries into the read-set assembly so session membership globs reach coverage['read_set'] (and thus hash_dep_entry/glob_membership_digest), rather than being dropped by normalize_read_set's existence filter.
evidence: terraform_seam._fold_usage folds membership globs into distinct_fetches via merge_synthetic_reads: `usage_sink["distinct_fetches"] = merge_synthetic_reads(fetches, concrete_reads=..., membership_globs=...)` (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/terraform_seam.py:269-272)

merge_synthetic_reads appends each membership glob as a read_file fetch: `merged.extend({"tool": "read_file", "target": t} for t in sorted(additions))` over both concrete_reads and membership_globs (src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py:282-287)

The read-set consumer only calls normalize_read_set on the unioned distinct_fetches: `normalized = normalize_read_set(fetches, base=_hash_basis(None))` (src/rebar/llm/workflow/plan_review_recovery.py:255)

normalize_read_set step 5 drops anything that is not an existing regular file: `if not os.path.isfile(resolved): return None` (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/read_set.py:170) — a glob string like `infra/**/*.tf` is not a file, so membership globs never reach coverage['read_set']

grep for terraform_membership_entries finds only its definition (read_set.py:189) and a unit test (tests/unit/workflow/test_terraform_plan_review_tools.py:153) — no production callsite wires it into _attach_read_set / read_set_dependency_paths / dependency_hashes

docs/grounding.md and ADR 0111 promise membership globs feed the signed read-set: `finalize() -> Usage ... report ... membership_globs (e.g. infra/**/*.tf) for the signed read-set` (docs/grounding.md session-API section)
dropped.finding: Terraform grounding membership globs are produced into distinct_fetches (as read_file targets) but never consumed into the signed read-set: normalize_read_set drops them at its existence filter, and the dedicated consumer terraform_membership_entries has no production callsite — so the documented 'membership freshness' attestation guard is not actually wired.
scenarios: A T10 grounding session reports membership_globs; after signing, a new .tf file is added under that glob — the attestation's freshness digest does not move because the glob was dropped from the read-set, so a stale review is treated as current.
Concrete .tf reads survive normalization (they are real files) but the membership-set guard the ADR relies on is silently absent.
dropped.suggested_fix: In _attach_read_set (or read_set_dependency_paths), route glob-shaped distinct_fetches targets through terraform_membership_entries and union them into coverage['read_set'] as glob dep entries, instead of relying solely on normalize_read_set which drops non-file targets.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the inlined generic `reason` enum in terraform_grounding_receipt.schema.json with a $ref to grounding.schema.json#/$defs/abstain_reason so the closed vocabulary has one source of truth.
evidence: terraform_grounding_receipt.schema.json:105-117 inlines the enum ["unsupported_lang","no_tool","parse_error","timeout","ambiguous","private_or_internal_suspected","network_error","rate_limited","version_skew","invalid_detector","other"]
grounding.schema.json:7-22 defines the same closed vocabulary as $defs/abstain_reason (byte-for-byte identical values/order)

schemas/__init__.py:441-454 registry() wires a cross-file referencing.Registry so a $ref to grounding.schema.json#/$defs/abstain_reason would resolve (the receipt schema already uses cross-file self-$refs, e.g. line 53 config_digest -> #/$defs/digest)

The receipt schema's `reason` field description at line 121 even states it 'mirrors grounding.schema.json's closed enum' — an explicit acknowledgement that this is a hand-copied mirror rather than a reference.
dropped.finding: terraform_grounding_receipt.schema.json re-inlines the generic grounding abstention `reason` enum (11 values) verbatim instead of $ref-ing the canonical source of truth grounding.schema.json#/$defs/abstain_reason; the two closed vocabularies can silently drift apart if the generic enum ever changes.
dropped.suggested_fix: In terraform_grounding_receipt.schema.json, change the `reason` property's first anyOf branch from an inline enum to {"$ref": "grounding.schema.json#/$defs/abstain_reason"}, matching how config_digest already $refs a shared def.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure the manifest pin, lockfile, and the `PARSER_VERSION` constant are kept in sync (or derive the expected version from metadata) so a version bump is a coordinated, tested change.
evidence: terraform_receipt.py: `PARSER_VERSION = "8.1.3"`
terraform_tools.py `_run_parse` passes `expected_version=tr.PARSER_VERSION` and `version=_installed_version()`
docs note: 'wrong parser version | `version_skew` / `parser_version`'
dropped.finding: The parser version is asserted in two independent places (code constant `PARSER_VERSION = "8.1.3"` and runtime `importlib.metadata.version("python-hcl2")`) with no single source-of-truth linking them to the manifest pin, so a manifest bump can silently diverge and trigger version_skew abstentions rather than a build-time failure.
scenarios: A dependency upgrade bumps python-hcl2 in the manifest but the code constant is not updated, causing every Terraform grounding query to abstain with version_skew
